scope: Research agent read primary repository code, licenses, documentation, papers and model metadata only. Integration phase downloaded and installed MIT en_core_web_sm 3.8.0 for offline hybrid NER. No patient datasets or SNUBH/MIDRC/CliniDeID weights downloaded.

installed_runtime_observed.implementation_scope: ko-pii and clinical rules plus local trained English spaCy tok2vec/NER; contextual generalization uses regex/dictionaries without LLM or embeddings.

sources.title: Marker-Inc-Korea/ko-pii
claims: Rules, dictionaries and checksums; core dependencies empty; package declares 1.16.0 and Python >=3.10.
No guarantee for arbitrary clinical free text, generic NER or legal anonymity.
reuse_conditions: Retain copyright and permission notice for copies or substantial portions.
sources.selection: Integrate pinned permissible core; measure domain-specific errors separately.

sources.title: ko-pii generalization modules
claims: generalize_age(47) returns 40대.
Korean 교수 maps to 연구/학계; unrecognized professor remains unchanged.
Anonymizer does not invoke sentence-wide exercise or family-history generalization.

sources.title: ko-pii encrypted Vault
claims: Optional cryptography AESGCM; 32-byte key and 12-byte nonce.
PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 480000 iterations, random 16-byte salt.
Vault mapping encryption does not itself supply app authorization or whole-original preservation after generalization.

sources.title: Data Privacy Stack Presidio (formerly microsoft/presidio)
sources.selection: HEAD source review only; actual integrated presidio-analyzer release is 2.2.360, recorded separately.

sources.title: Presidio language support and default model configuration
claims: Default models and recognizers are English; language-specific NLP and recognizer adaptation needed.
Default spaCy model is en_core_web_lg and ORGANIZATION is in labels_to_ignore.
PatternRecognizer.analyze can be called directly for patterns without loading a NER model; errors require representative evaluation.

sources.title: Presidio Encrypt operator
claims: Encryption/decryption operators are existing public features.
This file alone does not establish whole-input byte-exact restoration or the new capsule security properties.

sources.title: Explosion/spaCy en_core_web_sm 3.8.0 official release
sources.license: MIT (official versioned model release and metadata)
claims: English CPU pipeline includes trained tok2vec and NER; zero static word-vector entries does not imply absence of learned representations or ML.
General English NER evaluation cannot establish mixed Korean/English clinical PHI performance.
Integration explicitly selects installed en_core_web_sm 3.8.0 instead of default en_core_web_lg.
Model metadata cites OntoNotes 5 (commercial corpus licensed by Explosion), ClearNLP conversion and WordNet; source corpus conditions are not replaced by model MIT conditions.

sources.title: presidio-analyzer 2.2.360
claims: Actual installed version is distinct from 2026-10-08 reviewed repository HEAD.
Release source default YAML uses en_core_web_lg and ignores ORGANIZATION; app selects en_core_web_sm and uses explicit organization rules.
Retain the installed release's actual copyright and permission notice.
sources.selection: Actually connected in default hybrid detector via local spaCy NLP engine.

sources.title: spaCy 3.8.11
claims: Official package metadata labels MIT; actual local install version observed 3.8.11.
Version meets en_core_web_sm 3.8.0's >=3.8.0,<3.9.0 compatibility range.
sources.selection: Runtime NLP engine for integrated local English NER.

sources.title: De-identification of clinical notes with pseudo-labeling using regular expression rules and pre-trained BERT
claims: 51 regular expressions and pseudo-label fine-tuning of KoBERT-NER; six PHI categories.
Validation on 342 radiology and 12 non-radiology notes.
Paper reports regex P97.2/R93.7/F1 96.2 and fine-tuned KoBERT P96.5/R97.6/F1 97.1.
IRB policy prohibits sharing underlying data.
sources.metric_warning: Paper token/word evaluation is not current synthetic character-span evaluation; no direct score transfer or ranking.

sources.title: leelabsg/SNUBH_deid
sources.license_status: No LICENSE or explicit code redistribution permission located in the inspected README/tree; API license null.
claims: Default print_output writes idx, origin and transformed in plaintext CSV.
Repository lists model weights; existence is not a separately established redistribution permission.
sources.selection: Reference only; do not vendor, redistribute or download weights without permission.

sources.title: GitHub licensing a repository
claims: Without a license default copyright applies; public viewing/forking does not create a general reuse/derivative redistribution license.

sources.title: Stanford/Penn MIDRC Deidentifier
claims: Transformer PHI detection plus hide-in-plain-sight replacement.
README states research purposes only and cites JAMIA DOI 10.1093/jamia/ocac219.
reuse_conditions: Retain license and relevant attribution/NOTICE; label modified files.

sources.title: StanfordAIMI/stanford-deidentifier-base
claims: Official card labels English and MIT; model conditions differ from Apache-2.0 code.
No Korean/mixed clinical performance guarantee derived from card.
Source training data rights are distinct from card metadata.

sources.title: Clinacuity CliniDeID
sources.model_conditions: Pretrained machine-learning models may be used only for non-commercial applications.
claims: Java JDK17+ and models required; README beta has RNN component disabled.
Tagging and patient-record-consistent surrogate replacement described.
sources.selection: Comparison only; no model download or code integration.

sources.title: Beyond De-Identification: A Structured Approach for Defining and Detecting Indirect Identifiers in Medical Texts
claims: Nine indirect identifier categories; 100 MIMIC-III discharge summaries and 6199 annotations; baseline detectors.
Considers adversaries such as acquaintances, family members and medical staff.

sources.title: Clinical Text Anonymization, its Influence on Downstream NLP Tasks and the Risk of Re-Identification
claims: Analyzes anonymization effects across five downstream NLP tasks and a re-identification attack.
Supports separate utility/risk evaluation; does not establish this prototype's performance.
